knowledge:
- key_parameters: formula=The GLM formula used in the differential expression analysis (e.g., ~ Label) ;; .sample=The column name containing sample identifiers ;; .transcript=The column name containing transcript/gene symbols ;; .abundance=The column name containing read counts/abundance values ;; .significance=The column name containing P-values or significance metrics ;; .do_check=A logical column indicating which transcripts to check (e.g., FDR < 0.0001) ;; percent_false_positive_genes=The percentage of false positive genes tolerated (e.g., 5) ;; approximate_posterior_inference=Logical, whether to use approximate posterior inference (variational Bayes) or full MCMC ;; cores=Number of cores to use for multi-threading ;; draws_after_tail=Number of draws after tail (used to speed up execution in the vignette)
- alternatives: Standard negative binomial-based differential expression methods (like edgeR or DESeq2) which are not robust to extreme outliers. ppcseq is used as a post-hoc filter/check for these methods.
- when_to_use: Use this analysis when you have performed a differential transcript abundance analysis on RNA-seq data and want to identify and filter out false positive/inflated differential expression calls caused by single-sample outliers.
- pitfalls: Running without multi-threading on Linux can be slow; users should configure their ~/.R/Makevars with STAN_THREADS and pthread for speed. Setting draws_after_tail = 1 is only for speeding up vignette execution and may not be suitable for robust inference on real datasets.

workflows.name: outlier_identification_and_visualization
workflows.intent: Identify and visualize outlier transcripts from RNA-seq differential expression analysis results.
input: counts.tsv (A tidy tab-separated file containing sample IDs, transcript/gene symbols, abundance values, and differential expression statistics like P-value and FDR)
workflows.stages: 1. Load the tidy count and differential expression data ;; 2. Identify outlier transcripts using identify_outliers with a specified GLM formula and significance threshold ;; 3. Generate credible interval plots for the identified outliers using plot_credible_intervals
workflows.code:
counts.ppc = 
	counts %>%
	mutate(is_significant = FDR < 0.0001) %>%
	identify_outliers(
		formula = ~ Label,
		.sample = sample, 
		.transcript = symbol,
		.abundance = value,
		.significance = PValue,
		.do_check = is_significant,
		percent_false_positive_genes = 5, 
		approximate_posterior_inference = FALSE,
		cores = 1, 
		
		# This is ONLY for speeding up the Vignette execution
		draws_after_tail = 1
	)

counts.ppc_plots = 
	counts.ppc %>% 
	plot_credible_intervals() 

counts.ppc_plots %>%
	pull(plot) %>% 
	.[seq_len(1)]
